title: Work IQ: Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for agents
summary: The roadmap facts and the cited admin-center paths are supported. The spending-control automation needs correction: its GET request only lists policies and cannot set the spending limits the row describes.

claims.claim: Microsoft's documentation hub describes Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ is a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI

claims.claim: The Microsoft IQ hub lists four interconnected capabilities.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ brings together four interconnected capabilities:

claims.claim: The hub describes Work IQ as understanding how employees work, including people, collaboration and workflows.
claims.quote: Work IQ provides live understanding of how employees work, with context on people, collaboration, and workflows.

claims.claim: The hub describes Fabric IQ as providing the live state of the business.
claims.quote: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business, so agents understand business entities and their relationships, properties, actions, and rules.

claims.claim: The hub describes Foundry IQ as providing curated institutional knowledge.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge on the context of policies, authoritative documents, and reusable knowledge bases.

claims.claim: The hub describes Web IQ as providing fresh intelligence from the web.
claims.quote: Web IQ provides AI systems and agents with fresh, real-world intelligence from across the web.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly identified whether this roadmap release is the IQ hub, a Work IQ change or something else.
claims.quote: Searched: "570870" "Microsoft IQ"; "Work IQ" "Microsoft IQ" "570870" default licensing preview. Opened Microsoft IQ hub and Work IQ overview; neither ties its documentation to this roadmap release.

claims.claim: Work IQ enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context and tools.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.

claims.claim: Work IQ includes permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: It continuously builds a semantic understanding across Microsoft 365 and external systems with built-in, permission-aware governance.

claims.claim: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server and a REST API.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP tenant-policy documentation says mutation operations are not allowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: The separate Copilot Studio Microsoft Copilot harness guide says write operations are on by default.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.

claims.claim: A Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: The documented one-time Work IQ setup creates the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: The MCP overview says the Work IQ service principal is created automatically on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Manual service-principal provisioning can be needed to configure Work IQ MCP policy before first use.
claims.quote: In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP tenant policy path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control surface is tenant-level, not per-user, per-app, per-agent or scenario-template based.

claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies supplies the automation for the row's spending-policy control.
claims.quote: List spendingPolicies | GET /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies | Get a list of spending policies. ... Update spendingPolicy | PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} | Update a spending policy.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api.call with 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}' and api.docs with 'https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-update'. Add to its note: 'Set periodLimit in the request body to change the policy spending limit.' Update the rendered table accordingly. The existing GET only lists policies; the update reference documents periodLimit as writable.

claims.claim: The Cost Management API is beta, subject to change and not supported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.
